items.reason: Same agent: the record names 'boronophenylalanine, DMX-101' (BPA); borofalan (10B) is the INN for this moiety, so the INN form is preferred; moieties are re-mapped by script anyway.

items.proposed: no biomarker row (IDH not a selection biomarker)
items.reason: IDH appears only as WHO 2021 diagnostic categories ('Glioblastoma, IDH wildtype, WHO grade 4' alongside IDH-mutant astrocytoma); IDH-wildtype used to define GBM is excluded from molecular selection and is never candidate-matched.

'Investigational product, boronophenylalanine, DMX-101 500mg/kg/3hr' is a drug whose antitumour effect needs neutron irradiation (device: 'DM-BNCT'), the drug-device pattern of C12; no D30 ruling covers BNCT, and the radiation-only reading is possible since dose escalation is of radiation.
As for coder A: BPA is the registered 'Investigational product' activated by neutron capture; coded as drug-device candidate, pending XL view on whether BNCT is treated as radiotherapy only.
The only biomarker in question is IDH-wildtype used to define glioblastoma (Phase IIa 'Glioblastoma IDH-wild type, WHO Grade 4'), which is excluded from any_molecular_selection.

Neutron irradiation is registered as a Radiation intervention with dose escalation ('Radiation dose: 9 Gy-Eq'), so it counts as radiotherapy in the experimental arm; the alternative is to treat the beam as the activating device (as light in PDT).

Monotherapy requires 'no radiotherapy in the experimental arm'; each arm gives BPA 'followed by neutron irradiation to reach maximum brain dose of 9Gy-Eq', registered as [RADIATION]. Low confidence because under C12 the neutron beam could be seen as the activating device.

note: BNCT is not covered by any D30 ruling: decide whether boronophenylalanine (borofalan) with neutron irradiation is a device-dependent drug candidate (C12) or a radiotherapy-only trial (would fail S6). If it stays a candidate, decide whether the neutron beam is radiotherapy (regimen combination) or only the activating device (monotherapy).
